definition: The part of a retiree’s full benefit above the guaranteed 75%. It was paid separately by the Government and stopped after it said there was no funding beyond December 31, 2025.
The settlement’s promise that members receive at least 75% of their Full Benefits.
An expert who uses math and statistics to estimate how much a pension fund will need to pay, and for how long.
The actuary’s yearly check-up of the Fund: how many members there are, how much money there is, and how much the Government must pay.
A regular payment for life. Your monthly pension is an annuity.
A formal request asking the Settlement Fund to review a decision about your benefits. The Fund publishes its appeal rules, forms and fees.
The yearly investment earnings the plan expects over the long run. For the Settlement Fund it is 5.8%.
A person who receives benefits because of a member, such as a surviving spouse or child.
A lawsuit brought by a few people on behalf of a larger group with the same problem. Johnson v. Inos was a class action for retirees.
A retiree or beneficiary covered by the 2013 settlement.
A court order that records what both sides agreed to. Doc 562 in the settlement case.
Money paid into a pension fund, by the employee from each paycheck or by the employer.
A pension that promises a set monthly amount based on salary and years of service, rather than on how investments perform.
The court’s last decision in a case. Doc 561 approved the retirees’ settlement.
The pension a member would receive under the original Retirement Fund rules, before any reduction.
Money a fund holds divided by what it owes. 100% means fully funded.
Group Health and Life Insurance: the Government program that provides health and life insurance to employees and retirees.
What the Fund’s money earned over a period, shown as a percentage.
Government health coverage for people with low income. CNMI Medicaid: (670) 664-4880.
Federal health insurance for people 65 and older. Medicare: 1-800-772-1213.
The amount the Government must pay the Settlement Fund each fiscal year, set by the actuary. $29 million for FY 2026.
Marianas Public Land Trust, which holds public land money in trust. The Government has borrowed from it to meet budget needs.
Investment returns after the managers’ fees are taken out.
Paying each year’s benefits from that year’s budget instead of from savings. Expected for the Settlement Fund from about 2048.
A bill that has passed the Legislature and been signed by the Governor. Written like P.L. 24-20.
The NMI Retirement Fund, created in 1980. It ran short of money after years of unpaid Government contributions.
The 2013 agreement in Johnson v. Inos that created the Settlement Fund. Doc 468.
The NMI Settlement Fund, which took over Retirement Fund assets to pay class members at least 75% of Full Benefits.
The Annuity Recipient Information Update form. The Fund asks members to return it each year to keep payments going.
A pension paid to a member’s husband or wife after the member dies, generally 50% of the member’s benefit.
The independent person appointed by the court to oversee the Settlement Fund and report on it.
A former employee who earned the right to a pension but has not started receiving it yet.
